newsitem.title: USA: Centennial says probing results; fires chairman.
newsitem.headline: Centennial says probing results; fires chairman.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc., whose stock jumped more than fivefold last year, said Tuesday it was checking the accuracy of previously reported financial statements, and announced that its chief executive officer had been fired.

The manufacturer of personal computer cards and a contract maker of computer parts, said preliminary information has raised significant questions as to whether the reported results contained material misstatements.
Trading in Centennial's stock was halted on the New York Stock Exchange after it closed Monday at $16.375. By late afternoon, the stock had still not opened for trading.
Analysts said they expected the stock to open sharply lower, with one trader speculating it could open near $5 a share.
Last year, Centennial's stock jumped 451 percent, based on its closing price of $9.44 at year-end 1995 and $52 at the end of 1996.
The Billerica, Mass.-based firm said it was focusing on the earnings it reported for its fiscal second quarter ended Dec. 31 and financial statements for prior periods.
The board has appointed a special committee comprised of four directors to oversee the inquiry, it said.
Centennial said Emanuel Pinez, chairman, chief executive and secretary, was fired.
The company also said James Murphy was being relieved of his duties as chief financial officer until further notice and was assisting the company in its inquiry.

John Shields, vice-chairman of the board of directors, will chair the special committee. The special committee has engaged independent legal counsel to assist with the investigation, the company said, and independent auditors are assisting with this effort.
The special committee will also start a search for a CEO and an interim CFO. An article late last month in FinancialWorld questioned the company's accounting practices.
